label: Usability
summary: Usability here refers to how well a feature actually works in practice for the person trying to use it. In Maaike's work it shows up as a practical test: does this thing do what it promises? The ChatGPT browse feature is a case where the answer is no.
how_maaike_uses: Maaike uses usability as a reality check against hype. When she went to try the ChatGPT browse feature, she found it locked behind a data-collection toggle and, once enabled, described the browsing experience as subpar at best. So usability becomes a way to cut through the excitement around new features and ask whether they are actually worth using on their own terms, separate from the privacy trade-offs they come bundled with.
open_questions: Will the browse experience improve to the point where it becomes genuinely useful, and would that change the calculus around the data toggle?
If browsing through ChatGPT displaces traditional search engines, what does that mean for the volume and nature of data OpenAI collects?
